title: Would you use an 'Etsy witch'?
description:
Need good weather for your birthday? Want a date to go well? Maybe you’ve got exams coming up or want a promotion at work and need some good vibes. An 'Etsy witch' might be able to help…

There are loads of online witches on platforms, like eBay and Etsy, offering spells to help us with everything from love to money. But do they actually work? And why has witchcraft become so popular online?

Morgan from The Divine Eyes shop explains how she casts her spells, while we hear from people who’ve turned to online witches for help. Plus, William Lee Adams from the What in the World team explores the taboos surrounding witchcraft around the world.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討網路巫術以及在 Etsy 與 eBay 等線上平台販售咒語的流行趨勢。節目專訪在 Etsy 經營店家的賣家 Morgan 分享蠟燭儀式與心態轉變建議，並有買家分享購買成功咒語的體驗。此外，節目成員 William 指出美國巫術產業市值估計達 23 億美元，並說明 eBay 與 Etsy 對無形商品的規範，例如 Etsy 要求附帶實體產品。節目最後探討了經濟不確定性推動 WitchTok 的普及，以及巫術在沙烏地阿拉伯等國面臨的嚴格禁忌與法律規範。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart explores the rise of online witchcraft and spell-casting services on platforms like Etsy and eBay. Etsy witch Morgan explains how she performs candle rituals to foster mindset shifts for love and financial success, while a buyer shares how a success spell helped align their mindset for career opportunities. BBC's William Lee Adams details the $2.3 billion U.S. witchcraft industry, explaining e-commerce policies like eBay's ban on intangible spells and Etsy's requirement for tangible deliverables. The episode also discusses how economic uncertainty drives the popularity of WitchTok and contrasts modern online magic with severe anti-witchcraft laws in countries like Saudi Arabia.
